data.content_ref: inline:The target diagnoses the original dilemma as a 'false dichotomy created by a misunderstanding of probability' and proposes replacing 'probability of being true' with 'propensity to withstand tests.' But the target's own mechanism undermines this replacement: it defines the propensity as 'an existing dispositional property of the theory relative to the world.' A dispositional property grounded in the theory's relationship to reality just IS the theory's truth-approximation — so 'propensity to survive tests' collapses into 'propensity to be true.' The target thus commits the very fallacy it attributes to the dilemma: it creates a new false dichotomy between two notions that are functionally identical under its own definition. Its own countercondition ('Must distinguish clearly between propensity to survive tests and propensity to be true') is never satisfied; the target asserts the distinction exists but its mechanism provides no criterion that would separate them. If the disposition is objective and grounded in theory-world fit, surviving tests IS evidence of truth, and the original dilemma's inductive horn returns.
